plan.title: Plan and invite
plan.text: Start from a template or a plain checklist. Share out the tasks, send one link and collect replies per household — guests install nothing.

budget.title: Budget and deliver

day.title: Live the day itself

principles.title: Six rules we do not bend.
principles.lead: These are not advertising promises. They are how the product is built.

record.title: One record, many views
record.text: A task, a seat or a payment exists once. The list, the calendar, the floor plan and the event-day screen all show that same record, never copies of it.

preview.title: Preview before applying
preview.text: Moving the date, adding guests or swapping a supplier? “What if?” shows the effect on costs, deadlines and commitments first. Then you decide.

facts.title: Facts stay facts
facts.text: Arrivals, payments and received goods are never overwritten. They change only through a correction that stays in the history, so you always know what really happened.

unknown.title: Unknown stays visible
unknown.text: A missing price, an unmeasured dimension or a confirmation not yet received is written as “unknown”. We do not guess, we do not show zero, and we do not count it as done.

private.title: Private by default
private.text: Your guest list, budget and private requests are seen only by the people you have given that specific access.

paid.title: Paid means position, never preference
paid.text: Planning is free and carries no advertising. When paid promotion arrives in the directory it will be plainly labelled, will not change the order of other results, and will never enter your plan.

business.title: A directory where position is not for sale.
business.text: Venues, bands, caterers, florists, photographers: a listing is free, and so are the enquiries planners send you. During the launch period every business feature is free.

badges.title: Factual badges only
badges.meta: ONRC registration, insurance seen — no stars, no testimonials

closing.title: Your first occasion is waiting.
closing.text: Create an account with a code sent to your email. No password, no card, nothing to install.

meta.title: How it works
meta.description: A planner’s journey through EventDesk, step by step: an emailed sign-in code, tasks, invitations, budget, “What if?” and the day itself.

how.title: From an idea to “that was wonderful”, in seven steps.
how.lead: You do not have to take all of them. A small birthday needs three; a wedding needs all seven. The plan grows with the occasion.

account.title: Create an account in under a minute
account.text: Type your email address and receive a six-digit code, together with a link you can simply tap. There are no passwords to remember and we never ask for a card.

occasion.title: Create the occasion
occasion.text: Choose its kind — wedding, christening, birthday, party, trip — and start from a template or an empty list. A small occasion stays a simple checklist; a large one gains structure as you need it.

tasks.title: Share out the work
tasks.text: Every task has an owner and a due date. Invite collaborators who see only their part: the godmother looks after flowers, a friend after music, and you see everything.

invite.title: Invite people
invite.text: Send one link. Guests reply for their whole household, vote on the date if you have not fixed it, and can say what they will bring. They install nothing and create no account. Children are recorded as a number only, never by name.

budget.title: Keep budget and suppliers together
budget.text: Note what each thing costs, who pays and what is already settled. Quotes and conversations with suppliers stay in the plan, beside their orders and deliveries. Whatever you do not know yet stays written as “unknown”.

whatif.title: Check every change before you make it
whatif.text: Two more guests after the catering deadline? A new date? “What if?” shows what changes in costs, deadlines and tables. Nothing is applied until you confirm.

day.title: Live the day, then settle up
day.text: On the day, the run sheet is on your phone: what is next, who is on it, what has arrived. Afterwards you close the accounts, export what you want to keep and, if you wish, delete everything — with seven days to change your mind.

guest.title: One invitation, one question at a time.
guest.text: The guest opens the link and replies in a few taps: coming or not, how many adults, how many children, what they will bring. They can change their reply until the deadline you set, and always see what they promised.
guest.name: Sofia’s christening
guest.question: How many of you are coming?
guest.childrenHint: The number only. We never ask for names or ages.

free.a: Yes. Planners never pay, for any occasion. There is no trial period and we do not ask for a card. In future the service will be supported by businesses, through paid options that do not exist yet.

guests.a: No. They reply from a link, on any phone, without installing anything.

privacy.q: Who can see my guest list and budget?
privacy.a: Only you and the people you give that specific access. A business learns who you are only if you send it an enquiry, and sees only what you chose to share.

language.q: Can I use the app in English?
language.a: Yes. Romanian is the primary language and English can be chosen at any time, by guests too.

closing.title: The simplest thing is to try it.
closing.text: A first occasion takes a few minutes to create, and you can delete it whenever you like.

meta.title: For businesses
meta.description: A free listing in the EventDesk directory: how it works, what you get, and the rules of a directory where position cannot be bought.

business.title: Be found exactly when someone is looking.
business.lead: EventDesk has a business directory inside the plan itself. A planner who needs a venue, a band or a florist finds you at the very moment they are working on it. A listing is free. Enquiries are free.

launch.title: During the launch period, everything is free.
launch.text: For planners, for guests and for businesses — including every Business plan feature. There is no pricing page, no checkout, and we do not ask for a card.

listing.title: How a listing works.
listing.lead: Four things to know before you begin.

account.title: Create a business account
account.text: One account can hold up to five listings. Each listing picks one to five categories and up to twenty localities, across at most five counties.

lists.title: Choose from fixed lists
lists.text: Categories, counties and localities are picked from lists, never typed freely. A planner searching for “florists in Cluj” is sure to find you, and the directory stays tidy.

moderation.title: A moderator checks it
moderation.text: Every revision of a listing is approved by a moderator who is not a member of your business. While an edit is pending, the approved version stays public.

badges.title: You earn factual badges
badges.text: There are only two: “Verified: ONRC registration” and “Verified: insurance seen until” a stated date. The checks are free. There are no stars, scores or testimonials.

categories.title: The 21 categories
categories.note: The list is fixed at launch. Geography uses the 41 counties plus Bucharest.

get.title: Working tools, not just a shop window.

enquiries.title: Enquiries from planners
enquiries.text: A planner sends you a free enquiry with the kind of occasion, the date, the approximate number of guests, the area and, if they wish, a budget band. You learn about them only what they choose to tell you. You can answer with a PDF quote that they can accept straight into their plan.

drawings.title: Venue drawings
drawings.text: If you run a venue, upload its floor plan, calibrate it against a known distance and mark the tables, dance floor, bar, cloakroom and parking. Planners who work with you receive the plan in their occasion, to scale.

catalogues.title: Flower catalogues
catalogues.text: Florists publish their varieties with an image, season, colours and an indicative price per stem or bunch. Planners can ask for a quote starting from those very items.

plan.title: Business plan features
plan.text: Occasions owned by the business, worked on as a team with owner, admin and staff roles; shared libraries of templates, checklists and contacts; your logo and colour on guest pages; handing the occasion over to the client when it is ready. Free for the whole launch period.

stats.title: Your own statistics
stats.text: See how many views and enquiries your listing has had, as daily totals. We do not track individual visitors — not for you, and not for ourselves.

rules.title: An honest directory, stated plainly.
rules.lead: These rules will also be quoted in the business terms, so you know beforehand what you are signing up to.

organic.title: Organic order rotates daily and cannot be bought.
organic.text: No payment of any kind changes where a business sits among ordinary results.

launch.title: While the launch period lasts, there is no pricing.
launch.text: There is no pricing page, checkout or card entry anywhere in the product. There is no promoted placement either: the directory shows organic results only.

notice.title: “Featured — paid placement” will exist only after monetization is switched on.
notice.text: We give at least 60 days’ public notice, with reminders at 30 and 7 days. Nothing is charged automatically. A business that does nothing stays on the permanent free tier.

label.title: The label will be as visible as the business name.
label.text: Featured cards will sit above organic results, three at most, picked at random on every search, with the label set in the same size and weight as the name.

plans.title: Paid content stays out of plans.
plans.text: Featured content never appears in planners’ plans, on guest pages, in emails or in exports. Payment buys position in the directory and nothing else.

stars.title: No stars, no testimonials, no “recommended”.
stars.text: We show verifiable facts and let the planner choose.

free.title: What stays free for good.
free.text: The account, the listing, enquiries, venue drawings, catalogues and your own statistics. If the Business plan one day becomes paid and you do not take it, the occasions you already created remain fully usable.

unclaimed.title: Is your business already listed? You decide what happens next.
unclaimed.lead: Some listings are added by EventDesk from public sources — the Trade Register, the business’s own website or public pages — and approved by a moderator. They are minimal, strictly factual and carry the label “Added by EventDesk — not yet claimed”.

claim.title: Claim it
claim.text: Ask for a code, which we send to the contact address the business has published. If there is no public address, a moderator verifies the request against the public source. Once approved, the listing is yours, with every feature.

correct.title: Correct it
correct.text: If a detail is wrong, tell us which one and where we can find the right version. We correct it within 30 days.

remove.title: Remove it
remove.text: You can ask for the listing to be removed, or object to the processing, at any time. We act within 30 days and keep a record of the request, so the business is not added again.

unclaimed.note: An unclaimed listing shows only the contact route the business itself has published. It cannot receive enquiries through the platform, cannot be featured, and receives nothing from us except a single claim invitation by email — which says who added the listing and how to claim, correct or remove it. We send no marketing to contacts found this way, and we never use contacts entered by planners.
unclaimed.link: Claim, correct or remove a listing

closing.title: A listing takes a few minutes.
closing.text: Create an account with an emailed code, fill in the listing and send it for moderation. We do not ask for a card.
